newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares up 8 days in row on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares up 8 days in row on foreign buying.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.3 percent on Thursday to take their winning streak to eight days in a row and brokers said more gains were on the horizon.

"I reckon about half of the turnover of the past three weeks can be attributed to foreign investors who are especially interested in newly privatised firms like Lek, Kolinska and Droga," one broker said.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 3.23 points to 1,081.58.
* 10 shares rose and 10 fell, while four were untraded.
* Turnover eased to 309.7 million tolars from 371.9 million.
* Drug producer Lek's issue A had the highest turnover, firming 0.46 percent to 18,969 on volume of 6,864 shares for total turnover of 130.2 million tolars.

* Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, surging 38.45 percent to 30,058 tolars on volume of 177 shares for total turnover of 5.3 million tolars. Traders said the jump was purely a technical reaction to recent sharp falls.

* Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner, falling 2.81 percent to 17,105 on volume of 311 shares for total turnover of 5.3 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
